entities.summary: Roxana Moslehi is a renowned Iranian-born genetic epidemiologist who has made groundbreaking contributions to the field of genetics. Born in the 1980s in Tehran, Iran, Moslehi's early academic career was marked by her exceptional academic achievements, earning her a Ph.D. in genetics from a top-tier university. Her research focuses on the genetic epidemiology of infectious diseases, particularly in the Middle East, where she has conducted extensive work on the genetic determinants of resistance to tuberculosis. Moslehi's work has had a significant impact on the development of new diagnostic tools and treatments for infectious diseases, and her findings have been published in top-tier scientific journals. She is currently a leading researcher in her field and has received numerous awards for her contributions to genetics. Moslehi's work has also been recognized by the Iranian government, which has awarded her the title of 'National Hero of Science and Technology.' Moslehi's legacy extends beyond her scientific achievements, as she has inspired a new generation of Iranian scientists and researchers. Her story is a testament to the power of education, hard work, and dedication to one's field.
